note: Best-in-class open-source arsenal, one primary per job. Tools are DOWNLOADED at install time (never vendored). provision.py resolves the right per-OS asset live from each project's releases. Set GITHUB_TOKEN to avoid the 60/hr unauthenticated API limit.

tools.name: subfinder
tools.purpose: passive subdomain enumeration from 30+ OSINT sources

tools.name: dnsx
tools.purpose: DNS resolution, wildcard filtering, record queries, permutation

tools.name: naabu
tools.purpose: fast SYN/CONNECT port scan with host discovery
tools.runtime: SYN needs libpcap+admin; falls back to CONNECT unprivileged

tools.name: httpx
tools.purpose: HTTP liveness, status/title, tech detect, TLS, screenshots, raw replay
tools.runtime: PD binary; name collides with python httpx lib — call via bin/ path

tools.name: katana
tools.purpose: headless + passive web crawler, JS parsing (-jc)
tools.runtime: headless mode needs Chrome/Chromium

tools.name: gau
tools.purpose: historical/archive URL mining (wayback/CDX/OTX/URLScan)

tools.name: trufflehog
tools.purpose: secret detection over git/fs/JS with live credential verification

tools.name: tlsx
tools.purpose: TLS/cert intel: SAN harvest, JARM, issuer, expiry

tools.name: s3scanner
tools.purpose: enumerate + permission-check open cloud buckets (S3/GCS/Azure)

tools.name: wafw00f
tools.purpose: fingerprint the WAF/firewall in front of an app (150+ sigs)

tools.name: jsluice
tools.purpose: PARSER-based (not regex) extraction of URLs, endpoints, params and secrets from JS bundles + source maps
tools.runtime: no prebuilt release; needs Go AND a C compiler (CGO/tree-sitter). Builds on Linux/mac/WSL; on bare Windows (no gcc) it won't build — use WSL. Skill falls back to the regex/trufflehog path. Subcommands: jsluice urls|secrets <file.js>

tools.name: alterx
tools.purpose: subdomain permutation generator — feeds dnsx/puredns for ACTIVE bruteforce of the host surface

tools.name: subzy
tools.purpose: subdomain-takeover detection across 80+ service fingerprints (frequently-paid high/critical)
tools.runtime: no prebuilt release — needs Go toolchain

tools.name: x8
tools.purpose: hidden-parameter discovery in query/body/JSON/headers (Rust; finds inputs arjun misses)
tools.runtime: upstream's Windows asset is irregularly named (x86-windown-x8.zip) — matched via asset_overrides; no cargo needed

tools.name: feroxbuster
tools.purpose: recursive content discovery (Rust) with auto-recursion + smart filters — deeper than a single ffuf pass
tools.gate: noisy — rate-cap + leash it like ffuf

tools.name: kiterunner
tools.purpose: API-route content discovery from Swagger/OpenAPI + kitebuilder wordlists with correct methods/headers (where IDOR/BOLA live)
tools.runtime: binary is `kr`; needs a kitebuilder .kite wordlist (see data: kitebuilder)
tools.windows: no prebuilt Windows asset — the provisioner auto-builds it via go_fallback when Go is present (produces kiterunner, copied to kr); else use WSL.

tools.name: uro
tools.purpose: dedupe + collapse a URL firehose (gau/katana/archives) into unique, testable URLs — the quality gate before attack

tools.name: gf
tools.purpose: pattern-tag URLs for vuln-prone params (ssrf/redirect/sqli/ssti/lfi) using gf-patterns — prioritizes the attack queue
tools.runtime: needs Go toolchain; patterns from data:gf-patterns via GF_PATH

tools.name: graphw00f
tools.purpose: fingerprint the GraphQL engine behind an endpoint (routes the GraphQL attack playbook)

tools.name: puredns
tools.purpose: high-throughput DNS bruteforce + wildcard filtering (massdns front-end) — the heavy active-enum path
tools.runtime: requires massdns on PATH; default active-enum path is alterx|dnsx (no build). Use puredns for scale.

tools.name: massdns
tools.purpose: stub resolver powering puredns (C; must be compiled)
tools.build: cd bin/.src/massdns && make — binary at bin/massdns; Windows: use WSL or a prebuilt massdns

tools.name: nuclei
tools.purpose: template-driven vuln scanner (CVEs/misconfig/exposures/DAST) + OOB
tools.runtime: auto-pulls nuclei-templates (MIT) on first run; -dast + data:nuclei-fuzzing-templates turns it into a param fuzzer

tools.name: clairvoyance
tools.purpose: recover a GraphQL schema via field-suggestion even when introspection is DISABLED (unlocks BOLA/injection surface)
tools.runtime: no console script — call `python -m clairvoyance` via bin/.pyenv

tools.name: cent
tools.purpose: aggregate community nuclei templates into one dir (broadens nuclei coverage beyond the official set)

tools.name: ffuf
tools.purpose: fast web content/dir/vhost fuzzer, JSON output

tools.name: dalfox

tools.name: pspy
tools.purpose: read-only process/cron snooping that needs no root — a safe enumeration aid for internal-recon (P4)
tools.gate: read-only; runs on the foothold host via tools/leash-foothold.sh (Linux target only)

tools.name: pexpect
tools.purpose: drive a pty-bound interactive REPL/console (ssh/telnet/ftp client, a local challenge binary) via spawn/expect/sendline — the proto=pty path of leash-sock.py (P5)
tools.runtime: spawn() needs a Unix pty (Linux/mac/WSL); on Windows use pexpect.popen_spawn.PopenSpawn or WSL. Optional — only for proto=pty.

tools.name: websocket-client
tools.purpose: synchronous Python WebSocket tube (create_connection/send/recv) — the proto=ws|wss path of leash-sock.py (WS frames after the HTTP upgrade are invisible to the mitmproxy leash, so held + audited here) (P5)
tools.runtime: pure Python, cross-OS.

tools.name: websocat
tools.purpose: netcat/curl/socat for WebSockets (and raw TCP) — CLI manual exploration of a ws:// / wss:// endpoint (P5)
tools.runtime: single static Rust binary; prebuilt releases for all three OSes (or cargo install websocat).

tools.name: sourcemapper
tools.purpose: downloads a .map file (or reads local) and reconstructs the original source tree from sourcesContent — recovers un-minified TypeScript/JSX with comments, variable names, backend paths, test creds. Half of prod SPAs leak .map in 2026.
tools.runtime: Go toolchain required; single binary. Writes recovered tree to -output <dir>.

tools.name: webcrack
tools.purpose: unpacks webpack 4/5 + Browserify bundles into separate modules AND de-obfuscates obfuscator.io/JSFuck/unminify — turns chunks/1234.js back into readable src/components/Login.jsx so downstream jsluice/trufflehog work 10× more precisely.
tools.runtime: needs Node 22+. Releases every ~3 weeks. Output dir must be isolated per-run.

tools.name: asnmap
tools.purpose: expands an org name / ASN / IP / domain into ALL CIDR blocks the entity owns (IPtoASN data). Fills the gap subfinder/dnsx cannot — top-down discovery from a legal entity to its IP footprint. Pipes into naabu→httpx.
tools.runtime: requires free PDCP_API_KEY env var (projectdiscovery cloud free tier). Pure passive.

tools.name: webanalyze
tools.purpose: Go port of Wappalyzer using the community-maintained enthec/webappanalyzer dataset (continuation after Wappalyzer closed in 2023). Deeper tech+version fingerprint than httpx -tech-detect; concurrent 1-level crawl; JSON/CSV out. Key for hunting forgotten dev/staging builds with outdated stack.
tools.runtime: run `-update` before each engagement to refresh fingerprint dataset.

tools.name: bucketloot
tools.purpose: multi-provider bucket inspector — enumerates AWS S3 + GCS + DO Spaces + custom-URL (works against Alibaba OSS / Cloudflare R2 via S3-API endpoints) AND scans found objects for 80+ regex secret signatures. Closes the gap between s3scanner (S3 only, ACL only) and cloud_enum (name-only, no content).
tools.runtime: Go toolchain required. `-full` subcommand needs AWS creds for authenticated enum; unauth scan works keyless.

tools.name: wcvs
tools.purpose: dedicated Web Cache Vulnerability Scanner by Hackmanit — 10 web-cache-poisoning techniques + 3 web-cache-deception + CPDoS. Oracle-grade confirmation via persistence re-fetch (not generic header-reflection). JSON report. Opens a paid class nuclei does not cover.
tools.runtime: start with --threads 2 to avoid CDN flooding; -gr -gp for grouped JSON output.
tools.gate: noisy at high -tp thread; always run with threads cap + leash; safe for bb engagements that permit cache testing (verify scope).

tools.name: autoswagger
tools.purpose: harvests OpenAPI/Swagger specs, parses them, then replays EVERY endpoint expecting 401/403 — flags anything returning 200. Scans responses for PII (Presidio) + secrets (regex) + large-response leaks. Opens hidden-api + BOLA/BOPLA classes that wordlist-based kiterunner cannot reach.
tools.runtime: Python 3.7+; default scan is GET-only (safe). --brute mode gates behind operator approval (may trigger WAF or consume nonce).

tools.name: oasdiff
tools.purpose: diffs two OpenAPI/Swagger specs (the snapshots the fleet already harvested via katana/js/schema paths) and reports ADDED/changed/removed endpoints, params and auth requirements — catches new internal/debug routes and authz changes between releases that a one-time /swagger.json read misses. Deep-recon spec-diff, no arsenal equivalent.
tools.runtime: single Go binary (prebuilt per-OS incl. windows_amd64). `oasdiff diff -base old.json -revision new.json -f json`, or `oasdiff breaking` to isolate endpoint/authz changes.

tools.name: graphql-cop
tools.purpose: audits a GraphQL endpoint for known misconfigs BEYOND schema recovery — alias/batch overloading (DoS), field-suggestion leaks with introspection OFF, CSRF-via-GET, debug/trace modes, deep recursion. Complements graphw00f (engine fingerprint) + clairvoyance (schema recovery); does not duplicate them.
tools.runtime: python (pyenv); `python graphql-cop.py -t https://host/graphql -o json`. Target-facing → leash.

tools.name: smugglex
tools.purpose: request-smuggling / desync DETECTION (recon-grade, not exploitation): CL.TE/TE.CL/TE.TE, H2C and HTTP/2-downgrade (H2.CL/H2.TE), optional CL.0/0.CL + parser-discrepancy audits, JSON report + exit codes. Feeds class:request-smuggling hypotheses to the attack phase, where `smuggler` is the exploit tool.
tools.runtime: Rust, prebuilt release per-OS (smugglex-<v>-windows-x86_64.zip — no cargo needed). `cat urls.txt | smugglex -f json -o report.json`. DETECTION only; gate exploitation behind attack/request-smuggling scope. Target-facing → leash.
tools.gate: noisy — rate-cap + leash like any desync probe; verify scope permits smuggling tests.

tools.name: vulnx
tools.purpose: maps a detected stack (product+version from webanalyze/httpx) onto known CVEs enriched with EPSS score, CISA-KEV flag, nuclei-template availability and public exploit / HackerOne refs — turns a fingerprint into a PRIORITIZED exploitable-CVE list. Closes the CVE↔CPE gap with no arsenal equivalent.
tools.runtime: Go binary (prebuilt windows_amd64). `vulnx search 'product:<cms> && is_kev:true' -json`. PASSIVE (queries PD cloud, not the target) → direct, no leash. Full data uses the free PDCP_API_KEY (same token as asnmap/chaos); partial without.

tools.name: h1grep
tools.purpose: read-only CLI search over the PUBLIC HackerOne Hacktivity feed (keyword/program/severity/CWE/bounty) with no API key — gives novelty-scout/duplicate-scout raw prior-art data instead of hand-rolling the Hacktivity GraphQL, for the B3 dedup/prior-art pass.
tools.runtime:
pure Python single-file. `h1grep --query SSRF --program

--severity critical high --json`. PASSIVE OSINT — public feed only, no target traffic, no leash.

tools.name: unwaf
tools.purpose: WAF/CDN origin-exposure + behavioral divergence: discovers candidate origin IPs and compares origin-vs-edge behavior (HTML similarity, TLS fingerprint, headers) with a score — shows WHERE the WAF actually filters vs merely proxies. Goes beyond wafw00f (signature) + cdncheck (is-CDN).
tools.runtime: go install (no prebuilt release); needs the Go toolchain (present on this clone). `unwaf -d <host> --json`. Candidate-origin probing is target-facing → leash; passive edge lookups go direct.
tools.gate: GPL-3.0 — run-not-redistribute, same posture as puredns/uro/sqlmap already in this manifest.

tools.name: schemathesis
tools.purpose: property-based API fuzzing driven by the OpenAPI/GraphQL schema the fleet already harvested — generates edge-case + stateful (OpenAPI-links) requests and flags schema violations, unhandled 500s and state-mutation inconsistencies. Surfaces hypotheses a hand-fuzz of 10-20 fields never reaches.
tools.runtime: `schemathesis run <openapi-url> --checks all`; recon-grade use = conformance/5xx checks (read-leaning). Target-facing -> leash + rate-cap.
tools.gate: can send many requests and exercise mutating endpoints — rate-cap, leash, prefer non-mutating checks in recon; full fuzz is attack-scope.

tools.name: cachex
tools.purpose: web-cache-poisoning behavioral detector: sends unkeyed-header payloads, diffs baseline->poisoned, and CONFIRMS via a clean-request persistence re-fetch — distinguishes a weaponizable poisoning from header-reflection noise. Recon-grade detection feeding class:cache-poisoning to attack (where wcvs weaponizes).
tools.runtime: go install (no prebuilt release); Go toolchain present. `cachex -l urls.txt -m multi -j -o out.json`. Target-facing -> leash + rate-cap (CDN-flood risk).
tools.gate: sends cache-poisoning probes — leash + low threads; verify scope permits cache testing (same posture as wcvs).

tools.name: smtpeek
tools.purpose: SMTP recon deeper than nuclei network templates: VRFY/EXPN/RCPT user-enumeration with adaptive-delay + stealth modes, STARTTLS/implicit-TLS posture, banner/caps — read-only mail-surface mapping feeding the smtp-protocol lens.
tools.runtime: Rust; NO prebuilt release — `cargo install smtpeek` (or `cargo install --git https://github.com/0xricksanchez/SMTPeek`), binary copied into bin/. provision.py has no cargo method => reports 'manual'; one-time install. Non-HTTP -> tools/leash-tcp.sh, host-pinned, gated by policies.smtp_semantics_probe.enabled + max_recipients cap.
tools.gate: user-enumeration — respect the smtp_semantics_probe caps; never sweep a full user list.

tools.name: restler
tools.purpose: stateful REST API fuzzer that INFERS request dependencies from an OpenAPI/Swagger spec (create resource -> capture id -> reuse in a follow-up) and builds a stateful fuzzing grammar — the only arsenal tool that reconstructs multi-step API FLOWS (checkout/onboarding/multi-step forms), not just a flat route list. Surfaces use-after-free, broken sequence-authz and state-dependent bugs a one-shot fuzz misses.
tools.runtime: needs Python 3.8+ AND .NET 8 SDK. Build once: `git clone <git> && python restler-fuzzer/build-restler.py --dest_dir bin/.src/restler`; invoked as `dotnet bin/.src/restler/restler/Restler.dll <compile|test|fuzz-lean|fuzz|replay>` (bin/restler.cmd wraps it with the full dotnet path). provision.py has no dotnet-build method => reports 'manual'; one-time build.
tools.gate: INTRUSIVE — stateful fuzzing CREATES/DELETES real resources and sends many requests. Gate behind explicit scope permitting mutations (staging/test env); leash + rate-cap. Recon-grade use = `compile` + `test` (one pass per request, smoke) ONLY; full `fuzz` is attack-scope + operator GO.

tools.name: jwt_tool
tools.purpose: advanced JWT attacks beyond jwt-hack/flask-unsign: RS256->HS256 algorithm confusion (sign with scraped public key -> forge any identity -> ATO), jku/x5u header injection at an attacker JWKS, kid path-traversal/SQLi, none-alg + blank-signature, and -M exploit mode that replays against a live endpoint for the oracle.
tools.runtime: git clone + pip reqs (termcolor/cprint/pycryptodomex/requests/ratelimit) via pyenv; wrapper bin/jwt_tool. `bin/jwt_tool <JWT> -X k -pk pubkey.pem` (alg-confusion), `-X i -I -hc kid -hv ...` (header-inject), `-M at -t <url>` (live exploit). GPL run-not-redistribute, like sqlmap/uro/puredns. Target-facing replay -> leash.

tools.name: wafrift
tools.purpose: WAF/filter bypass WEAPONIZER (the mutation layer smugglex/unwaf/wafw00f detect but cannot bypass): metaheuristic search (hill-climb/annealing/tabu/MAP-Elites) over an encoding-ladder (URL/Unicode/HTML-entity/chunked) + grammar (SQLi/XSS/cmdi/SSTI/SSRF/LDAP/path-trav) + content-type (JSON/XML/multipart) + parser-differential mutation space until a payload passes Cloudflare/Akamai/Fastly/Imperva/F5/AWS-WAF; also smuggle-emit (CL.TE/TE.CL/TE.TE desync requests), discover, ja3-diff. JSON/SARIF out.
tools.runtime:
Rust, prebuilt release (wafrift--x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip -> no cargo needed; cargo install wafrift-cli as fallback). `wafrift scan --target --payload "

" --param --format json -o r.json`. Feed ONE payload/param; cap concurrency. Target-facing -> leash. ja3-diff/--tls-impersonate need MSVC+cmake (present).
tools.gate: noisy mutation search -> rate-cap + leash; verify scope permits WAF-bypass probing.

tools.name: ysoserial-net
tools.purpose: .NET deserialization RCE gadget generator (CRIT class with ZERO prior arsenal coverage): ViewState/BinaryFormatter/LosFormatter/ObjectStateFormatter/Json.NET/DataContractSerializer gadgets -> unauth SYSTEM on ASP.NET/IIS. Inert generator (you deliver the payload through Spider's own leashed HTTP probe + interactsh oracle with a benign id/whoami command).
tools.runtime: MANUAL (multi-file: ysoserial.exe + sibling DLLs — the single-binary github-release path would strip the DLLs). Extracted whole into bin/.src/ysoserial.net/, wrapper bin/ysoserial-net.cmd -> the exe. Native .NET (dotnet 8 / .NET Framework present). `bin/ysoserial-net -g TypeConfuseDelegate -f Json.Net -c "cmd /c whoami" -o base64`. Generation inert; delivery via leash.

tools.name: phpggc
tools.purpose: PHP object-injection / unserialize() gadget-chain generator (~150 chains: Laravel/Symfony/WordPress/Magento/Drupal/Monolog) -> RCE, arbitrary file write, SQLi via a reflected unserialize sink. The PHP half of the deser gap (phar:// too).
tools.runtime: MANUAL (needs the PHP CLI, installed via winget PHP.PHP.8.3). git clone into bin/.src/phpggc/, wrapper bin/phpggc.cmd -> php phpggc. `bin/phpggc Monolog/RCE1 system id -b`. Inert generator; delivery via leash.

tools.name: ysoserial
tools.purpose: Java deserialization RCE gadget generator (the canonical builder the deser SKILL names): CommonsCollections1-7/Spring/ROME/C3P0/Hibernate chains -> readObject/JMX/RMI/JNDI sinks. Inert generator; delivery via leash + interactsh oracle.

Credential control-test (nuclei default-logins, netexec) is gated behind policies.default_cred_control_test.enabled and runs ONLY through tools/leash-cred.sh (spray-not-brute, capped, lockout-aware, one host pinned — never a range, never --continue-on-success past a one-pass spray; no hydra/medusa). Last-mile objective extraction (P1: exiftool/imagemagick/binwalk) runs LOCALLY on an already-downloaded in-scope artifact — no network, no leash; only the download goes through the leash. CTF solve tools (P3: pwn/rev/crypto/forensics/stego, all optional:true + phase ctf-<cat>, provisioned with `python arsenal/provision.py --phase ctf-<cat> --optional`) run on a PROVIDED, in-scope artifact analysed locally/offline; a pwn remote delivery is host-pinned via tools/leash-tcp.sh (one host:port, never a range); factordb/online crypto lookups are OPT-IN egress of public params only; nothing here attacks a third party. Post-foothold tools (P4: peass-ng, gtfobins/lolbas data, pspy) run ONLY on a host where a shell:<host> capability is oracle-proven, through tools/leash-foothold.sh (host-pinned, non-destructive denylist, bounded loot); linPEAS stealth profile only; NO persistence/implant tooling. Interactive-protocol exploitation (P5: held socket/REPL) runs ONLY through tools/leash-sock.py (host-pinned via guard.py, frame/byte/session-time capped = anti-flood, full transcript to raw/), gated behind policies.interactive_protocol.enabled; pwntools/pexpect/websocket-client/websocat are OPTIONAL ergonomic drivers — the wrapper core is pure stdlib; never raw netcat a target.
